etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Borrowed from Latin fortunatus.

Morphologically fortune +‎ -ate.

quote.citation: 1854, Edward Stanley, A Familiar History of Birds : Their Nature, Habits and Instincts‎[1], page 144:
quote.text: if it sits still, with its breast towards them, till they have passed, they consider it as a fortunate sign, and everything is expected to go on well during the remainder of their journey

definitions.definition: Happening by good luck or favorable chance.

quote.citation: 2011, George G. Szpiro, Pricing the Future: Finance, Physics, and the 300-year Journey to the Black-Scholes Equation‎[2]:
quote.text: How many lucky winners, Regnault lamented, boastfully ascribe their success to wise decisions while in reality their triumph was nothing more than the fortunate outcome of random events?

quote.citation: 2018 July 11, “How Nina Weiner turns dreams into a reality”, in The Jerusalem Post:
quote.text: Weiner acknowledges that a stroke of good luck has helped steer her to a more fortunate path early on in life.
